$comment: Written by `agentic-factory init`. Every project-specific value lives here; the handbooks, templates and scripts read it. Never put secrets in this file.

rhythm.$modes: day-plan-night-build: the human plans, tests and decides by day, the Controller builds unattended at night, morning handover; continuous: the Controller builds whenever signed-off work exists and asks as questions arise; custom: quietHours define when the Controller may start new work

steering.$modes: github-issues: tickets are GitHub issues with labels; orca-tasks: tickets are docs/tasks/T<n>-*.md files
steering.$readyCheck: enforce: the Controller takes only a ticket that is ready to code (status ready, an Assessed: line with a ready outcome, goal, acceptance criteria, limits, level, no unanswered blocking open question), and stops one that is not before a worker starts for it. warn: the same check, but a ticket that is not ready to code is still taken, with a message; this is what a project without the key gets. One case is refused in either setting, so after `update` it changes what an existing project does: in github-issues mode an issue that carries needs-info, also next to the ready label, is no longer listed or claimed; remove the label once it is answered. A ticket already in progress is never stopped. See docs/workflow.md, Sharpen the ticket.

context.$sources: Where the Front agent finds what answers a ticket's open points, stated once, in general terms: the overall specification, other documents, material of a predecessor project or an earlier system. A list of paths, links or short descriptions; the factory assumes no layout. Read by the Front agent at the sharpen-the-ticket step.

hosts.$comment: A remote server is an option, not a must. The controller runs on one host (the local machine or a remote one). Workers run on zero or more hosts; each has its own paths, Orca environment and capacity. With no remote hosts everything runs locally.

controller.$wake: idleMinutes: an idle project (no new inbox line, worker message or finished wave, no ready ticket, no running worker) is woken at most this often. busyPointerMinutes: a Controller that Orca reads as busy gets a one-line pointer to what is waiting after this long. repeatMinutes: an unanswered pointer, or a wake typed because the Controller marked itself waiting (cycle.mjs end), is typed again after this long. quietSeconds: its terminal must have printed nothing for this long for that marker to be believed. dialogPatterns: regular expressions (case-insensitive, per line) matched against the last 8 lines of the Controller's screen; while one matches, nothing is typed (Enter would take the default). After dialogHoldMinutes the Front agent is told that the Controller seems to wait at a dialog, once and again only when the question changes. The values shown are the defaults.
controller.$hung: A Controller that is busy, whose terminal keeps changing, and whose status.md and journal did not change for 'minutes' is reported to the Front agent. restart: only true lets the heartbeat restart it (once, after 'restartAfterMinutes', if its terminal shows the same frame twice and no wave, gate or push runs); the default false reports only. patterns: regular expressions that, visible for patternMinutes, also count as hung (report only); none are shipped. resetAfterDays: a restart this long ago no longer counts as 'restarted once'.
controller.$restart: contextPercent: the Controller starts itself fresh (restart.mjs) after a wave or when idle once its context use is above this share. contextGapMinutes / minGapMinutes: restart.mjs refuses a restart sooner than this after the last (asked by the Controller / any other). afterGateMinutes: no restart this soon after a gate, wave or push.

stall.$stall: Optional, for stallwatch.mjs: how long one worker-show call (asking Orca whether a worker waits for a human) may take, and how long all of them may take per host and cycle. The screens are judged first, so these never delay the stall judgement. The values shown are the defaults.

frontAgent.$kind: terminal (default): the Front agent is an agent session in a terminal, woken by statuswatch.mjs; orca-bot: an Orca bot on this machine is the Front agent, woken by one Orca automation with a precheck (botwatch.mjs). One bot can serve several projects: name the same bot in each.
frontAgent.$bot: orca-bot only: the bot's name as `orca bot list` shows it. Create the bot in Orca first; start creates its watch automation.
frontAgent.$staleMinutes: How old the Controller's status.md may get before the Front agent is told (the bot's watch wakes the bot once; the terminal watch alerts once). null: hosts.controller.wake.idleMinutes + 15 minutes (45 by default). An idle Controller is woken only every wake.idleMinutes and refreshes status.md then, so a value below idleMinutes + 15 is raised to that, and doctor and the watch say so: set this at least that high, or null.

preview.$worktree: Optional "worktree": where the preview clone lies when PREVIEW_WORKTREE puts it somewhere other than ~/Development/<project>-preview, so that capacity.mjs counts what runs there as the project's own load.

agents.$runners: orca: workers run in Orca worktrees and terminals; terminal: workers run as plain codex/claude/pi processes in git worktrees
agents.$askOff: Optional, per agent CLI: how a worker starts with its ask-the-user tool off with the terminal runner, e.g. { "claude": { "args": ["--disallowedTools", "AskUserQuestion"] } }. The args go right after the executable and must not end in a variadic option. An entry replaces the built-in one of that agent; null removes it. Built in: claude only. Under the orca runner nothing can be passed to the agent, so this has no effect there. For pi there is no built-in entry: with the terminal runner pi runs without a UI, where ask extensions already refuse. A project on pi 0.77.0 or later may set { "pi": { "args": ["--exclude-tools", "ask_user_question,question,questionnaire"] } }; the entry replaces, it does not extend, so repeat every name you want off. A pi that does not know the flag may exit with an unknown-option error instead of starting: set it only when every worker host has the flag. See docs/orca.md.
agents.$askPatterns: Optional regular expressions (case-insensitive, per line) matched against the last 8 lines of a worker's screen by stallwatch.mjs; a match on an idle prompt skips the 90 s idle wait. Off by default.
agents.$piRoleModels: Optional, e.g. { "Developer": "provider/model-id" }: a Pi worker of a listed role starts pinned to that provider/model instead of its tier's model. Other roles and other agents keep their tier. An explicit --model still wins.
agents.$calibration: The model names are examples of what the agent CLI offers; init asks for the available ones. auto: calibrate-models.mjs moves a role one tier down when its pass rate is high and rounds are low, one tier up when failures cluster; manual: it only recommends.

capacity.$comment: Defaults for every worker host; a host's own capacity block overrides single values.
capacity.$classes: Two capacity classes. light: Developers. heavy: Testers and every other writing worker, and what runs full gates. Without PSI (macOS) a heavy start is allowed up to load1 = threads x heavyLoadPerThread, a light one up to threads x lightLoadPerThread. With PSI (Linux) heavy uses pressure.cpuAvg10MaxPercent and light pressure.lightCpuAvg10MaxPercent, which, when not set, is cpuAvg10MaxPercent x lightLoadPerThread / heavyLoadPerThread (33 with the defaults), at most 13 above the heavy limit and below 100; 0 is refused. The factors 0.9 and 1.5 are starting values not yet backed by measurement. See docs/capacity.md.
capacity.$lightUnattributed: Above the heavy CPU limit a light start needs an attributed load: foreign plus unknown load at most threads x this value, and readable at all; otherwise light falls back to the heavy limit. 0 switches the condition off.
capacity.$foreignLoad: Foreign load (CPU cores used during a one-second sample by processes working in another git checkout) holds a start only when it is above threads x foreignLoadMaxPerThread AND load1 is at least threads x foreignLoadMinLoadPerThread (below that the host is clearly not busy; 0 switches this second condition off). As a reason it never lowers a calibrated cap (overload that foreign work causes still does). Processes whose owner cannot be told are reported as unknown; they never hold a start as foreign load, but a large unknown load takes away the light class's extra room.

calibration.$comment: The caps above are starting values. auto: start low (startSuite), raise by step while the host stays quiet for raiseAfterQuietMinutes at the cap, lower on pressure or load timeouts; the audit verifies. manual: use the configured caps as they are.

commands.$docsChecks: Optional. formatCheck (e.g. a formatter's check mode such as "prettier --check .", run through the project's own tooling) and markdownCheck (e.g. "markdownlint-cli2 '**/*.md'") are what a wave of documentation alone runs instead of verify and e2e (docsOnly.enabled); a task's wave never qualifies (its spec review, report and status branch are in it), so they matter little; an empty one is skipped.
commands.$formatStaged: Optional, off when empty: pre-commit runs this formatter in write mode on the staged files (paths appended) and stages the result, e.g. "prettier --write --ignore-unknown" run through the project's own tooling. Or { "command": "…", "paths": ["**/*.py"] } to pass only matching files. Partially staged files keep their unstaged changes.

docsOnly.$enabled: true: a change that touches documentation only (tools/factory-guardrails.mjs docs-only, fail closed) and whose ticket says so itself (Level: 1 and Documentation only: yes, both when the work started and when the check runs) gets no Tester (the ticket's own spec review and report, new files, do not count against it); its wave still runs the full gates once (only a wave of documentation alone, with none of a task's process files in it, runs commands.formatCheck and commands.markdownCheck instead). Read from the main branch's factory.config.json, so it takes a reviewed change to get it there (agentic-factory init asks once; later it is a ticket: the factory's docs/testing.md). false: every change takes the full path.
docsOnly.$paths: Where documentation lives (** any depth, * and ? within a directory, {a,b}); each pattern starts with a directory name or names top-level files. Only plain Markdown and raster images count; the files the factory installs or reads as process state (protocols, coordinator and workflow docs, reviews, tickets), agent instruction files, dot paths and executable files never do. Read from the main branch: a change cannot widen its own allowlist.
docsOnly.$extraTypes: Opt-in file types that can carry code: "svg", "mdx". Empty: Markdown and raster images only.

cleanup.$pendingWarnMinutes: How long removable work may wait before status and doctor report it. cleanup.mjs deletes only with --apply; a run without it records since when something waited (cleanup-pending.json in the Controller directory), and a run with --apply clears that. Default 30.
